Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},

   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),

                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:

Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.

result.name: Intuitive Surgical, Inc.
result.industry: Robotic-assisted surgery systems and instruments (medical devices)
markets: Robotic-assisted soft-tissue surgery (da Vinci Xi, da Vinci 5, da Vinci SP)
Surgical instruments, staplers and energy accessories used per procedure
Service contracts and digital/training tools for installed robots

mission.statement: We believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
mission.source: Intuitive careers website, 'Who we are' page (careers.intuitive.com, 2026); the FY2025 10-K also states 'we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care.'
mission.plain: Intuitive builds smart tools that let doctors operate through tiny cuts so patients heal faster and live better.

about.plain: Intuitive makes robots called da Vinci that help surgeons do operations through a few small cuts instead of one big one. The surgeon sits at a console and moves tiny robotic arms holding thin tools and a 3D camera. Every operation uses special Intuitive tools that are thrown away or replaced, so the company earns money each time the robot is used. It also makes Ion, a robot with a thin bendy tube that reaches deep into the lungs to check spots for cancer.
about.customers: Hospitals and surgery centers around the world buy or lease the robots and then buy the tools and service for every operation.
about.everyday: If someone you know had their prostate, uterus, gallbladder or part of a colon removed with 'robotic surgery', it was very likely done on a da Vinci robot.

money.plain: the tools, staplers and supplies used in every robotic operation (H1 2026 share)
da Vinci and Ion robots sold or leased to hospitals (H1 2026 share)
service contracts, repairs and support for installed robots (H1 2026 share)

money.part: da Vinci 5 (launched in the US in 2024)
money.plain: newest robot with force feedback and more computing power; 870 placed in 2025
robot for reaching small lung nodules to diagnose cancer early; procedures up about 51% in 2025

money.part: Single-port surgery and digital/AI tools (da Vinci SP, case insights)
money.plain: one-incision robot and data tools that could open new procedures and services

result.summary: Intuitive has one of the widest moats in medical devices: more than 12,000 da Vinci systems installed worldwide, over 20 million procedures performed, and a razor-and-blade model where about 76% of H1 2026 revenue came from recurring instruments, accessories and services. Surgeons trained on da Vinci, hospital workflows built around it and decades of clinical data create strong switching costs, though Medtronic's Hugo (FDA-cleared December 2025) and J&J's Ottava (FDA De Novo July 2026), plus cheaper Chinese robots, are the first real challenges in the US and China.

pricingPower.evidence: In Q2 2026 instruments and accessories revenue rose 17.7% ($1,734.9M vs $1,474.1M) against about 15% da Vinci procedure growth, as da Vinci 5 lifted spend per case, and non-GAAP gross margin rose to 70.0% from 67.9% despite a guided 1.0%-of-revenue tariff hit; 2025 gross margin was 66.0% on $10,064.7M revenue. Pricing pressure exists in China, where management cited policy-driven price cuts and domestic competition in July 2026.

moats.evidence: 'da Vinci' is the brand surgeons and patients associate with robotic surgery, backed by thousands of patents, FDA clearances across many procedures and a large body of peer-reviewed clinical evidence built over 25+ years.

Hospitals have sunk capital, trained surgical teams and built OR workflows around da Vinci; surgeons who learned on da Vinci rarely switch, and the 11,710-system installed base (June 30, 2026, +12% y/y) drives proprietary instrument and service purchases.

More installed systems mean more trained surgeons, residency programs, published outcomes and procedure data (over 3.15 million da Vinci procedures in 2025), which in turn attract more hospitals; it is an indirect, data and training network rather than a pure user network.

With $10.06B of 2025 revenue and $1,311.8M of R&D (more than most rivals' entire robotics revenue), Intuitive spreads R&D, manufacturing (Mexico, US, Germany) and a global service force over a far larger base than any competitor.

Soft-tissue surgical robotics needs huge R&D, clinical trials and service networks, so only a handful of well-funded firms (Medtronic, J&J, CMR, Chinese players) have entered after two decades of Intuitive dominance.

Intuitive is the incumbent; rivals such as Hugo (modular carts) and Ottava (table-integrated) try to counter-position on cost and footprint, though usage-based leasing (131 of 254 operating lease placements in Q2 2026) helps Intuitive answer on price.

Decades of iteration in robotics, precision instrument manufacturing, surgeon training pathways and hospital-program support (e.g., moving from Xi to da Vinci 5 with force feedback) is very hard for newcomers to replicate quickly.
Its large pool of da Vinci-trained surgeons and a clinical evidence database across millions of procedures function as a semi-exclusive asset, though key early patents have expired.

customers.evidence: Hospitals keep adding systems: da Vinci placements rose to 1,721 in 2025 from 1,526 in 2024 and to 468 in Q2 2026 from 395, with 246 da Vinci 5 placements in the quarter, many as trade-ins and expansions at existing customers; procedure volume (the best loyalty signal) grew about 18% in 2025.

talent.evidence: Intuitive lists Glassdoor Best Places to Work 2026, TIME Americas Best Companies 2026 and Forbes America's Dream Employers 2025 among its awards; it had about 17,021 employees at end 2025 with 9.3% turnover (FY2025 10-K).

product.evidence: da Vinci is the most widely used and most clinically studied soft-tissue surgical robot, with over 20 million procedures worldwide and broad multispecialty indications; da Vinci 5 adds force feedback, and Ion leads robotic bronchoscopy, while Hugo and Ottava have narrower initial US clearances (urology; general surgery).

competitors.name: Medtronic
competitors.note: Hugo RAS system, FDA-cleared for urologic procedures in December 2025, already sold in many markets outside the US; also a major supplier of surgical staplers and energy devices.

competitors.name: Johnson & Johnson (J&J MedTech)
competitors.note: Ottava table-integrated soft-tissue robot received FDA De Novo authorization in July 2026 for general surgery; its Monarch platform competes with Ion in robotic bronchoscopy.

competitors.name: CMR Surgical
competitors.note: UK private company selling the modular Versius robot, mainly in Europe, India, Latin America and other non-US markets.

competitors.name: Shanghai MicroPort MedBot
competitors.note: Toumai soft-tissue robot competing in China (and seeking exports), benefiting from China's domestic-preference tenders.

competitors.name: Shenzhen Edge Medical
competitors.note: Chinese maker of multi-port and single-port laparoscopic robots competing for Chinese hospital tenders; listing status not verified.

competitors.name: Medicaroid (Kawasaki Heavy Industries / Sysmex joint venture)
competitors.note: hinotori surgical robot sold in Japan and parts of Asia.

competitors.name: SS Innovations International
competitors.note: Low-cost SSi Mantra robot targeting India and other price-sensitive markets.

competitors.name: Noah Medical
competitors.note: Galaxy robotic bronchoscopy system competing with Ion in lung biopsy.

competitors.name: Karl Storz
competitors.note: German private endoscopy leader that acquired Asensus Surgical (Senhance robot) in 2024; competes in laparoscopy and visualization.

competitors.name: Distalmotion
competitors.note: Swiss private maker of the Dexter robot, positioned for ambulatory surgery centers and hybrid laparoscopy.

competitors.name: Shandong Weigao Group Medical Polymer
competitors.note: Chinese surgical robot developer named by Intuitive as a competitor in China.

competitors.name: meerecompany
competitors.note: Korean maker of the Revo-i surgical robot.

competitors.name: Stryker
competitors.note: Mako robot dominates orthopedic joint replacement, a different segment; competes for hospital robotics budgets.

threats: Medtronic Hugo (US urology clearance December 2025) and J&J Ottava (US general-surgery De Novo July 2026) giving hospitals credible alternatives and price leverage
Chinese domestic robots (MicroPort Toumai, Edge Medical and others) plus volume-based procurement and lower tender activity eroding share and price in China
GLP-1 obesity drugs reducing US bariatric surgery volumes, and expiry of enhanced ACA subsidies softening deferrable US procedures (cited on the July 2026 call)
Tariffs on instruments made in Mexico, endoscopes from Germany and Chinese materials (about 1.0% of revenue in 2026 guidance)
Hospital capital budget pressure slowing system placements
Third-party instrument reprocessors and antitrust litigation challenging limits on EndoWrist instrument reuse
Valuation risk: the stock traded about 49x trailing earnings in October 2026, leaving little room for slower procedure growth

ceo.name: David (Dave) Rosa
ceo.background: Mechanical engineer (B.S., Cal Poly, 1989); Intuitive's ninth employee (1996), led engineering, clinical development, the teams behind da Vinci SP and Ion, then president from 2023 before becoming CEO on July 1, 2025

c1.evidence: Intuitive created and leads robotic soft-tissue surgery, a still-young field where da Vinci procedures grew about 18% in 2025 to roughly 3.15 million and are guided up 13.5-15.5% in 2026.

c2.evidence: Hospitals choose da Vinci for its clinical track record (20M+ procedures), trained surgeon pool, broad indications and service network; this ecosystem took 25+ years to build and is hard for Hugo or Ottava to copy quickly.

c3.evidence: 'da Vinci robot' is widely recognized by patients and is the default in robotic surgery, but the Intuitive company name itself is far less known to the general public than consumer brands.

c4.evidence: Its stated belief that 'minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care' runs through filings and investor talks, and management emphasizes patient outcomes and lower total cost of care; another decade of shifting open surgery to minimally invasive would matter to millions of patients.

c6.evidence: “robotic surgery, high-tech, premium, expensive”: the public largely associates da Vinci with advanced, less painful surgery, a mostly positive impression tempered by cost concerns and past product-liability lawsuits.

c7.evidence: Only a minority of the millions of eligible soft-tissue surgeries worldwide are done robotically, and aging populations plus the shift to minimally invasive care keep the addressable market growing; revenue rose from $4,358.4M in 2020 to $10,064.7M in 2025.

c8.evidence: Expansion paths include new procedures (general surgery, thoracic, cardiac with da Vinci 5), single-port SP, Ion lung biopsy, international markets, ambulatory surgery centers and digital/AI tools.

m1.evidence: Dave Rosa articulates a long-term vision of data-driven, less invasive care and personally started the groups that produced SP and Ion, but he is a newer CEO (July 2025) rather than a widely known visionary.

m2.evidence: Rosa is not a founder but joined in 1996 as employee number nine and has spent about 30 years building the company, acting like a long-term owner-operator.

m4.evidence: The CEO-transition release stressed Rosa's 'patients-first focus', and Intuitive's strong Glassdoor 'Best-Led Companies' recognitions suggest employee-oriented leadership, though direct evidence of servant leadership is limited.

m5.evidence: Intuitive's engineering-led culture has kept inventing new platforms (Xi, SP, Ion, da Vinci 5), and Rosa himself founded the clinical engineering, endoluminal and 'Future Forward' groups.

m6.evidence: Rosa is a Cal Poly mechanical engineer who led engineering, clinical and product development before becoming CEO.

m7.evidence: Leadership consistently frames its work around patient outcomes and lower total cost of care, and there are no notable character controversies, but evidence beyond corporate statements is limited.

m7b.evidence: No record found of Dave Rosa giving a commencement address at a top university.

m8b.evidence: Rosa is a low-profile, engineering-focused executive rather than a public personality.

m9.evidence: As president and then CEO he oversaw the da Vinci 5 launch (870 placed in 2025) and revenue growth from $7,124.1M in 2023 to $10,064.7M in 2025, with Q2 2026 revenue up 19%.

m10.evidence: Intuitive is known for heavy investment in R&D, manufacturing and training rather than for frugality; SG&A was $2,385.0M in 2025.

c10.evidence: Over 20 million da Vinci procedures worldwide have given patients smaller incisions, less pain and faster recovery, across urology, gynecology, general and thoracic surgery.

p2.evidence: Building surgical robots safe enough for millions of operations, with precision instruments, 3D vision and force feedback, is extremely hard, as shown by rivals taking a decade or more to reach the US market.

f2.evidence: Operating margin rose from 24.1% in 2020 to 29.3% in 2025, but gross margin was 65.6% in 2020, peaked at 69.3% in 2021 and was 66.0% in 2025.

f3.evidence: Intuitive has no debt, $8,625.5M of cash and investments at June 30, 2026, $3,030.5M of 2025 operating cash flow and $18,297.7M of shareholders' equity.

f4.evidence: Operating income rose from $1,049.8M in 2020 to $2,945.5M in 2025 and operating cash flow from $1,484.8M to $3,030.5M, despite a dip in 2022.

v1.evidence: da Vinci has by far the most clinical evidence, trained surgeons and approved procedures; an ordinary patient can see that their surgeon has most likely trained on it and that it is the most proven robot.

v2.evidence: Intuitive cites Glassdoor Best Places to Work 2026, TIME Americas Best Companies 2026, Glassdoor Best-Led Companies 2025 and Forbes America's Dream Employers 2025.

c5.evidence: Thousands of hospitals and the surgeons who perform over 3 million da Vinci procedures a year would be hard hit, and patients would lose an established less-invasive option for many cancer and other operations.
